claim: Semantic Entropy Probes (SEPs) approximate semantic entropy directly from the hidden states of a single model generation, eliminating the need to sample multiple generations at test time.
stance_target: cheap single-pass approximations can recover the sampling-based uncertainty signal
scope_conditions: general LLM hallucination detection (QA-style tasks), not code generation
quoted_support: To address this, we propose SEPs, which directly approximate SE from the hidden states of a single generation. SEPs are simple to train and do not require sampling multiple model generations at test time, reducing the overhead of semantic uncertainty quantification to almost zero.

claim: Full semantic entropy (SE) computation via sampling incurs a 5-to-10-fold increase in computation cost relative to a single generation, which hinders practical adoption.
stance_target: sampling-based confidence is accurate but expensive
quoted_support: the 5-to-10-fold increase in computation cost associated with SE computation hinders practical adoption.

claim: SEPs retain high performance for hallucination detection and generalize better to out-of-distribution data than prior probing methods that directly predict model accuracy.
stance_target: hidden-state probes are a viable cheap proxy for sampling-based uncertainty
scope_conditions: general LLM tasks tested in the paper, OOD generalization explicitly claimed
quoted_support: We show that SEPs retain high performance for hallucination detection and generalize better to out-of-distribution data than previous probing methods that directly predict model accuracy.

claim: Ablation studies indicate that specific token positions and model layers of hidden states capture semantic-entropy-relevant information, implying the SE signal is linearly recoverable from internal representations.
stance_target: single-pass hidden states encode enough information to approximate multi-sample semantic uncertainty
quoted_support: our ablation studies give further insights into the token positions and model layers for which this is the case.

claim: SEPs are not validated on code generation tasks in the published abstract, leaving a domain gap between general-QA hallucination detection and code-LLM confidence calibration.
stance_target: existing single-pass UQ methods lack code-domain validation
scope_conditions: based on abstract-level description; full paper not yet confirmed
quoted_support: We show that SEPs retain high performance for hallucination detection and generalize better to out-of-distribution data than previous probing methods that directly predict model accuracy.
